summary: Laura Harrington is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, as well as Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., and several other teachers.

Lauran Hartley is a scholar of Tibetology. She has held positions as an adjunct lecturer at Columbia University, visiting assistant professor at Indiana University, teacher at Rutgers University (attested 2003), and consultant and editor at Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003).

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a medical degree from the University of Glasgow (~1874–1878), served in the Indian Medical Service (~1879–1917), and was Professor of Tibetan at University College London (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon (1869–1943) was a scholar of Japanology and Sinology. He studied at Trinity College, Oxford (~1888–1892), worked at the British Museum (~1893–1933), and held a post at Harvard University (~1933–1934).

Laurence Khantipalo Mills (1932–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under teachers including Jianmin Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, Sangharakshita, and Dudjom Rinpoche, and served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978.

Laurie L. Patton (1961–) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago (~1986–1991) and held posts at Emory University (~1996–2011), Duke University (~2011–2015), and Middlebury College, serving as president from 2015 to 2024.

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar of religious studies. His appointments include Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions (attested 2000), Professor at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004), and Professor of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at institutions including Butler University, Indiana University, and New York University, completing a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2012).

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1895–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903), where he was taught by Maurice Bloomfield.

Leah Zahler (1936–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) as well as Harvey B. Aronson and Ngawang Wangyal.

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He was Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University (attested 2011) and a Research Associate in anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution (attested 2011).

Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She completed a PhD at the University of Michigan (until 2005) under doctoral supervisors Luis O. Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College.

Leo Frobenius (1873–1938) worked in history and archaeology. He held posts at the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), the Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938), and the Berlin Society for Anthropology, Ethnology, and Prehistory.

Leo M. Pruden (1937–1991) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1964–1966) under Akira Hirakawa, and previously under Taitetsu Unno (1960). His posts included Brown University (1970–1971) and the Nyingma Institute (1971).

Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (1849–1852) under Theodor Benfey and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851–1854). He held posts at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Tartu (1865–1899).

Leo Strauss (1899–1973) was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Marburg, Hamburg, and Freiburg. His career included posts at the University of Cambridge (~1934–1938), The New School (~1938–1949), and the University of Chicago (~1949–1969).

Leon Hurvitz (1923–1992) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (~1955–1971) and subsequently at the University of British Columbia (~1971–1989), continuing there until ~1992.

Leonard Bloomfield (1887–1949) was a linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Francis Asbury Wood (1908–1909). He held professorial posts at Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago (1927–1940), and Yale (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé (1946–) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Leiden University (~1965–1970) and later held a post there from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and teacher F. E. L. Priestley, and held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).
